investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Swarm Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100) in Production
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing in production with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval cannot provision a new agent to validate VM readiness or runtime state, so no required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is being collected.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard cap of 100 agents per org (or globally, scope unclear from evidence). At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T19:15:56Z), that limit was already at capacity, causing POST /api/agents to return 409 with "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the eval's first step — agent creation — is blocked, all downstream assertions (vmIdPresent, remoteState) cannot be evaluated. This is a quota/capacity exhaustion condition on the swarm layer, not a code defect in the agent creation API itself.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null} at 2026-06-14T19:15:57.732Z
Sibling check remote-agent-state failed with identical 409 message at 2026-06-14T19:15:58.722Z
Sibling check remote-agent-runtime failed with identical 409 message at 2026-06-14T19:15:59.765Z
All three checks share the same error payload verbatim, confirming the failure is at the shared agent creation step, not in per-check downstream logic
Eval latency was 1383ms (well within the 30000ms warning and 120000ms outage thresholds), ruling out a timeout as the cause
Expected output contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], but no evidence object was populated — consistent with creation being blocked before any VM is assigned
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] The swarm org-level or global agent quota of 100 is exhausted by live or leaked agents that were not cleaned up by prior eval runs or production workloads, preventing any new agent from being created

[Medium confidence] The AURA eval harness creates a new agent on each run but does not reliably delete it afterward (e.g., on prior run failure), causing quota to accumulate over repeated eval cycles until the limit is hit
[Medium confidence] A separate production workload or tenant sharing the same quota namespace recently scaled up agent usage to the 100-agent ceiling, coincidentally blocking the eval

[Lower confidence] The swarm backend's quota counter is stale or incorrectly incremented (e.g., counting terminated/deleted agents as still active), making the quota appear exhausted when actual live agents are below 100

investigation.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exceeded (HTTP 409) Blocking All Remote Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval environment's agent quota is at or above the 100-agent hard limit, preventing the eval harness from provisioning a new agent to run any downstream state or runtime checks.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard quota of 100 agents per org/environment. At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T19:15:57Z), the production eval environment had already reached or exceeded this limit. Every POST /api/agents call — regardless of which check issued it — was rejected with HTTP 409 and the inner error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because all three checks depend on successfully creating a new agent as their first step, none could proceed to collect the required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing a full sweep failure across the remote-agents feature checks. This is an eval-environment resource exhaustion issue; no evidence in the supplied data indicates a broader production user-traffic outage.
proof: All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) returned identical HTTP 409 error bodies: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The inner swarm error explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the hard limit has been reached.
All three failures occurred within a 2-second window (19:15:57Z–19:15:59Z), consistent with a shared quota state rather than independent transient errors.

The failedCheck evidence object is empty ({}) and the expectedOutputContract required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are all absent, confirming no agent was ever created and no downstream state could be collected.

Latencies for all three failing calls (990 ms, 1383 ms, 1043 ms) are well below the warning threshold (5000 ms) and outage threshold (20000 ms), indicating the 409 was returned promptly by the quota enforcement layer — not a timeout or infrastructure failure.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The eval harness creates a new agent on every run but does not reliably clean up (delete) agents after each run, causing agents to accumulate in the production eval environment until the 100-agent quota is exhausted.
[Likely] A previous eval run or series of runs failed mid-execution (e.g., after agent creation but before teardown), leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota.
[Possible] The eval environment shares an org-level agent quota with real production workloads or other automated processes, and concurrent usage from those sources has consumed the available quota.
[Less likely] The swarm backend's quota limit (100) is misconfigured or too low for the volume of eval runs expected in this environment, causing quota exhaustion under normal eval cadence.
[Less likely] A bug in the eval check logic causes it to attempt agent creation even when a suitable agent already exists, unnecessarily consuming quota slots.

investigation.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exceeded (409 Conflict) Blocking All Remote Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously at 2026-06-14T19:15:57–59Z with identical 409 Conflict responses indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. The eval harness cannot provision a new agent to run its test lifecycle, so no expected-output contract assertions (e.g., "hello from aura" message) can be evaluated.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend is returning "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on POST /api/agents, meaning the org-level agent quota is exhausted. The eval harness depends on being able to create a fresh agent at the start of each check run; because creation is blocked, every downstream check (state, runtime, chat readiness) also fails. This is a quota/resource exhaustion condition in the swarm layer, not a code defect in the agent runtime itself. Whether this reflects leaked eval agents from prior runs, a production quota shared with eval, or a genuine org-level saturation is not determinable from the supplied evidence alone.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 on all three sibling checks: remote-agent-create (endedAt 2026-06-14T19:15:57.732Z), remote-agent-state (endedAt 2026-06-14T19:15:58.722Z), and remote-agent-runtime (endedAt 2026-06-14T19:15:59.765Z).

All three 409 responses carry the identical error body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The inner swarm error explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the org has reached its maximum allowed concurrent swarm agents.

Latencies for all three failing calls (1383 ms, 990 ms, 1043 ms) are well within the warning threshold (20000 ms) and outage threshold (60000 ms), confirming the API itself is responsive — the failure is a business-logic rejection, not a timeout or infrastructure outage.

The expected-output contract requires evidence fields orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message, plus an assertion that message contains 'hello from aura' — none of these can be satisfied because agent creation never succeeded.
possibleCauses: (Highest likelihood) Eval harness agents from previous runs were not cleaned up, causing accumulated agents to exhaust the 100-agent quota over time. Each eval cycle creates an agent but a prior failure or missing teardown step left it alive.

(High likelihood) The eval environment shares the same org-level agent quota as production or staging workloads, and concurrent real usage has consumed the remaining quota slots, leaving none available for eval provisioning.
(Medium likelihood) A prior eval run crashed mid-lifecycle (after create, before delete), leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota but are not visible to the eval harness.
(Lower likelihood) The quota limit of 100 is misconfigured or too low for the combined eval + production load on this org, and the limit itself needs to be raised.
(Lower likelihood) The swarm backend is misreporting quota state due to a stale cache or counter drift, causing it to reject creation even if fewer than 100 agents are actually active.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Fails: Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable (404) — SESSION_OPEN_FAILED
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed immediately (2127ms) because the agent runtime returned a 404 when the stream attempted to open a session, emitting a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error frame before any progress or completion frames could be produced. Both required evidence fields — frameTypes (containing generation_completed) and imageUrlPresent — are absent, confirming the stream never advanced past session initialization.
investigation.rootCause: The agent runtime harness is unreachable at the configured endpoint (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL). The 404 response indicates either the harness process is not running, the deployment is missing or misconfigured, or the eval environment is pointing to a stale or incompatible harness version that no longer exposes the expected route. This is an infrastructure/configuration failure in the eval environment, not a confirmed production user-traffic outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failedCheck.evidence.frames[1].event = 'generation_error' with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED, confirming the stream aborted at session-open time.
failedCheck.evidence.frames[1].data.message explicitly states 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version.'
failedCheck.message confirms both required evidence fields are missing: frameTypes and imageUrlPresent.
Stream produced only 3 frames: generation_start, generation_error, and an empty message frame — no generation_progress, generation_completed, or artifact URL frames were ever emitted.
latencyMs of 2127ms is far below the warningLatencyMs threshold (180000ms), consistent with an immediate connection failure rather than a timeout or slow generation path.
failedCheck.status = 'fail' in environment: production (eval environment), with no sibling check failures or user-traffic signals supplied.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The harness process is not running or was never started in the eval environment — the 404 is returned immediately, indicating no listener at the target route.
[Likely] LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL environment variable is misconfigured, pointing to a wrong host, port, or path that does not match the deployed harness route.
[Likely] The harness was deployed at an incompatible version whose API routes differ from what the eval client expects, causing the specific session-open endpoint to return 404.
[Possible] A recent deployment or infrastructure change removed, renamed, or gated the agent runtime endpoint, breaking the route the eval client calls to open a session.
[Less likely] A network-layer issue (firewall rule, DNS misconfiguration, proxy) is intercepting the request and returning a synthetic 404 before it reaches the harness.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Fails: Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable (404) — SESSION_OPEN_FAILED
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed immediately (2127ms) because the agent runtime returned a 404 when the stream attempted to open a session, emitting a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error frame before any progress or completion frames could be produced. Both required evidence fields — frameTypes (containing generation_completed) and imageUrlPresent — are absent, confirming the stream never advanced past session initialization.
investigations.rootCause: The agent runtime harness is unreachable at the configured endpoint (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL). The 404 response indicates either the harness process is not running, the deployment is missing or misconfigured, or the eval environment is pointing to a stale or incompatible harness version that no longer exposes the expected route. This is an infrastructure/configuration failure in the eval environment, not a confirmed production user-traffic outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

failedCheck.evidence.frames[1].data.message explicitly states 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version.'
failedCheck.message confirms both required evidence fields are missing: frameTypes and imageUrlPresent.
Stream produced only 3 frames: generation_start, generation_error, and an empty message frame — no generation_progress, generation_completed, or artifact URL frames were ever emitted.
latencyMs of 2127ms is far below the warningLatencyMs threshold (180000ms), consistent with an immediate connection failure rather than a timeout or slow generation path.
failedCheck.status = 'fail' in environment: production (eval environment), with no sibling check failures or user-traffic signals supplied.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The harness process is not running or was never started in the eval environment — the 404 is returned immediately, indicating no listener at the target route.
[Likely] LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL environment variable is misconfigured, pointing to a wrong host, port, or path that does not match the deployed harness route.
[Likely] The harness was deployed at an incompatible version whose API routes differ from what the eval client expects, causing the specific session-open endpoint to return 404.
[Possible] A recent deployment or infrastructure change removed, renamed, or gated the agent runtime endpoint, breaking the route the eval client calls to open a session.
[Less likely] A network-layer issue (firewall rule, DNS misconfiguration, proxy) is intercepting the request and returning a synthetic 404 before it reaches the harness.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Swarm Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100) in Production
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing in production with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval cannot provision a new agent to validate VM readiness or runtime state, so no required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is being collected.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard cap of 100 agents per org (or globally, scope unclear from evidence). At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T19:15:56Z), that limit was already at capacity, causing POST /api/agents to return 409 with "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the eval's first step — agent creation — is blocked, all downstream assertions (vmIdPresent, remoteState) cannot be evaluated. This is a quota/capacity exhaustion condition on the swarm layer, not a code defect in the agent creation API itself.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null} at 2026-06-14T19:15:57.732Z
Sibling check remote-agent-state failed with identical 409 message at 2026-06-14T19:15:58.722Z
Sibling check remote-agent-runtime failed with identical 409 message at 2026-06-14T19:15:59.765Z
All three checks share the same error payload verbatim, confirming the failure is at the shared agent creation step, not in per-check downstream logic
Eval latency was 1383ms (well within the 30000ms warning and 120000ms outage thresholds), ruling out a timeout as the cause
Expected output contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready], but no evidence object was populated — consistent with creation being blocked before any VM is assigned
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] The swarm org-level or global agent quota of 100 is exhausted by live or leaked agents that were not cleaned up by prior eval runs or production workloads, preventing any new agent from being created

[Medium confidence] The AURA eval harness creates a new agent on each run but does not reliably delete it afterward (e.g., on prior run failure), causing quota to accumulate over repeated eval cycles until the limit is hit
[Medium confidence] A separate production workload or tenant sharing the same quota namespace recently scaled up agent usage to the 100-agent ceiling, coincidentally blocking the eval

[Lower confidence] The swarm backend's quota counter is stale or incorrectly incremented (e.g., counting terminated/deleted agents as still active), making the quota appear exhausted when actual live agents are below 100

investigations.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exceeded (HTTP 409) Blocking All Remote Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval environment's agent quota is at or above the 100-agent hard limit, preventing the eval harness from provisioning a new agent to run any downstream state or runtime checks.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard quota of 100 agents per org/environment. At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T19:15:57Z), the production eval environment had already reached or exceeded this limit. Every POST /api/agents call — regardless of which check issued it — was rejected with HTTP 409 and the inner error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because all three checks depend on successfully creating a new agent as their first step, none could proceed to collect the required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing a full sweep failure across the remote-agents feature checks. This is an eval-environment resource exhaustion issue; no evidence in the supplied data indicates a broader production user-traffic outage.
proof: All three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) returned identical HTTP 409 error bodies: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The inner swarm error explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the hard limit has been reached.
All three failures occurred within a 2-second window (19:15:57Z–19:15:59Z), consistent with a shared quota state rather than independent transient errors.

The failedCheck evidence object is empty ({}) and the expectedOutputContract required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are all absent, confirming no agent was ever created and no downstream state could be collected.

Latencies for all three failing calls (990 ms, 1383 ms, 1043 ms) are well below the warning threshold (5000 ms) and outage threshold (20000 ms), indicating the 409 was returned promptly by the quota enforcement layer — not a timeout or infrastructure failure.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The eval harness creates a new agent on every run but does not reliably clean up (delete) agents after each run, causing agents to accumulate in the production eval environment until the 100-agent quota is exhausted.
[Likely] A previous eval run or series of runs failed mid-execution (e.g., after agent creation but before teardown), leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota.
[Possible] The eval environment shares an org-level agent quota with real production workloads or other automated processes, and concurrent usage from those sources has consumed the available quota.
[Less likely] The swarm backend's quota limit (100) is misconfigured or too low for the volume of eval runs expected in this environment, causing quota exhaustion under normal eval cadence.
[Less likely] A bug in the eval check logic causes it to attempt agent creation even when a suitable agent already exists, unnecessarily consuming quota slots.
